cands.bio: Democrat and Vietnam veteran who has represented northern Bay Area districts in the U.S. House since 1999 and sits on Ways and Means. Former California state senator (1990-1998), vineyard owner, winery maintenance supervisor, and college instructor. Incumbent in California's 4th District.

endorsements.text: U.S. Sens. Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries endorsed Thompson in 2026.
Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, IUOE Local 3 and Equality California endorsed Thompson in 2026.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance or action by Thompson on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, police pay and pensions, school choice or teacher pay. We found nothing on his own Second Amendment record beyond his statements, and no documented controversies in the pages we could read. His campaign issues page was cut off partway through, so the water section is incomplete. Details of his state Senate record, including his own account of chairing its Budget Committee, could not be checked against official legislative records.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

second-amendment.evidence: Says he supports Second Amendment rights for law-abiding owners but wants comprehensive criminal background checks on all commercial gun sales, and says he wrote and introduced a bipartisan bill to require them.

workers-first.evidence: Calls for comprehensive immigration reform with a pathway to citizenship for long-resident families, protections for DREAMers, and a guest worker program for agricultural workers. He also says he has supported some enforcement measures.

pro-life.evidence: Described as pro-choice despite being Catholic; he opposed the overturning of Roe v. Wade, calling it 'an assault on women'.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Opposes the Bay Delta Conservation Plan as flawed and not science-based, saying it would harm Delta farmers, fishermen, communities, wildlife and the environment.

cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California's 4th Congressional District. Yale graduate, former partner at Dragoneer Investment Group, and co-founder of the American Dream Institute and the Rachel and Eric Jones Foundation. Grew up in rural Maine and now lives in Napa with his wife and two children.
cands.gaps: We could not find where or when Eric Jones was born, the year he moved to California, or the dates of his work at Dragoneer Investment Group. He has held no public office, so there is no governing record to report. We found no stated positions or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration or H-1B visas, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. The campaign pages we had were cut off partway, so some of his platform and personal story is unread.
